title: Russian Cosmonaut Tells KCG Students What Space Exploration Really Demands
summary: Test cosmonaut Nikolai Tikhonov spoke on the mental and physical preparation behind spaceflight at Science Festival India 2026, hosted by KCG College of Technology, Chennai.
body_html:
Chennai, 21 October 2026: Space exploration demands mental resilience and physical endurance as much as scientific knowledge, Russian test cosmonaut Nikolai Tikhonov told students at Science Festival India 2026, hosted by KCG College of Technology, Chennai.

The festival was organised by the Russian non-profit organisation Energy of the Future with the support of Rosatom State Atomic Energy Corporation. The inaugural ceremony was attended by Aleksandr Fomin, Vice Consul and Deputy Chief of Mission, Consulate General of the Russian Federation in Chennai; Daria Korzheva, organiser of the festival; Dr. Annie Jacob, Director, KCG College of Technology; Dr. G. Prabhakaran, Principal; and Dr. K. V. Narayanan, Director – Operations.

In his lecture, titled Space Is Calling, Tikhonov spoke about nuclear technologies in space and the training needed for human spaceflight. He explained how isolation, confined living spaces and microgravity place stress on cosmonauts, and how training builds emotional stability, quick reflexes and sound judgement. Videos of parachute exercises and zero-gravity training showed how cosmonauts learn to perform under pressure. He also described a selection process that includes more than 180 examinations.

"Initiatives such as Science Festival India 2026 give students the opportunity to engage with international experts and understand the real-world challenges that shape scientific discovery," said Dr. Anand Jacob Verghese, Chairman, Hindustan Group of Institutions.

Dr. Annie Jacob said such collaborations "provide students with valuable opportunities to learn beyond the classroom" and inspire them "to think beyond boundaries".

The festival also included a career session on nuclear education pathways with Shri R. S. Sundar, former Executive Director (Operations), NPCIL; Ivan Ushakov, Senior Lecturer, Tomsk Polytechnic University; and student ambassador Srivignesh Poonaram. Ushakov lectured on nuclear medicine, and Prof. Sivasankaran Bijoy Nandan of Cochin University of Science and Technology spoke on ocean exploration.

The festival ended with science debates on atomic technologies in space and everyday life, in which students of KCG College of Technology and Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science took part.
